clue.text: Starts in college, having accepted post as fellow

indicators.note: the starts of the next four words, college through post, are the letters wanted here

explanation.surface: A new arrival at a college takes up a teaching post as a fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starts in' takes the opening letters of college, having, accepted and post; 'as' links to the definition, so 'fellow' is not the college rank but a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal words for a man, a bloke or guy.

clue.text: Inhuman and boring routine in research site set up

indicators.note: in means the routine goes inside the upturned research site
in a down clue, set up means the word for the research site is written upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: a lab, short for laboratory, is a place for research
a rut is a dull, unvarying routine

explanation.surface: Work in a laboratory is described as dull and cruel, perhaps animal testing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' looks like drilling but means tedious; in a down clue 'set up' writes the lab upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: something savagely cruel lacks human feeling.

clue.text: From launch, fish — abandoned little ones

parts.note: to launch an enterprise is to found it
lings are long cod-like sea fish

explanation.surface: Baby fish abandoned straight after launching from the spawning ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names infants left by unknown parents and found by others, children abandoned.

clue.text: Play lead in Othello as famous actor

parts.note: Brand is a verse drama by Ibsen

indicators.note: lead in means the first letter of the following word, Othello

explanation.surface: An actor is invited to take the title role in Shakespeare's Othello.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' looks like a verb but is a noun: BRAND is Ibsen's verse play. Add O, the first letter of Othello.
explanation.definitionFit: Marlon of that surname was a celebrated Hollywood actor, star of The Godfather.

clue.text: Male is held up, secured by an academic in strong grip

indicators.note: something secured by another piece is held inside it

parts.note: a don is a university teacher
he is the male pronoun

indicators.note: in a down clue, held up means the word is written upwards, so read backwards

explanation.surface: A man is held up in a strong grip by a lecturer, a scuffle on campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held up' looks like delayed or robbed, but in a down clue it turns 'is' upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: the noun names the quality of sticking fast, a firm hold.

clue.text: Remove from board of firm or suspend officially

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the words that follow, across their boundaries

explanation.surface: Someone is to be removed from a company board, or suspended officially.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across 'boarD OF Firm'; the setter adds 'or suspend officially', where 'suspenD OFFicially' holds it equally, a second hiding place offered as an alternative.
explanation.definitionFit: To take off a hat or garment is to remove it; a synonym in that sense.

clue.text: Old part of Spain in centre — and central part for 4

indicators.note: in means the old Spanish region is placed within the word for centre

parts.note: the core of something is its centre
Leon was an old kingdom of Spain, now a region

explanation.surface: Instructions for locating a historic region of Spain in the middle of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: '4' points to the actor at 4 down; the part is his famous film role.
explanation.definitionFit: Marlon Brando played Vito, the Godfather of the surname, his central role in the film.

clue.text: Behave very heartlessly in a lot of larks

indicators.note: heartlessly means each of the two words loses its inner letters, keeping only the ends

explanation.surface: Someone behaving very callously while getting up to a lot of larks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'larks' looks like pranks, but here they are birds.
explanation.definitionFit: The collective noun for a flock of larks, or quail, is a group of that name.

clue.text: Sheltered in shady spot he had located outside

indicators.note: he had sits outside, wrapping round the shady spot

parts.note: he had is contracted to he'd
an arbour is a leafy, shaded bower in a garden

explanation.surface: A man took shelter in a shady garden spot he had found.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to give harbour to is to shelter or protect.

clue.text: Element not in usual form — wrongly ordered an ounce

indicators.note: the two pieces from an ounce are put in the other order

parts.note: an means one

explanation.surface: A chemist finds an element in an odd form because an ounce was mixed up in the order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly ordered' here is a simple swap of the two pieces, not a full jumble of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an allotrope of oxygen, three atoms per molecule instead of the usual two.

clue.text: Applied, turned down

indicators.note: turned means the phrase for down is read backwards

parts.note: down is the same as not up

explanation.surface: Something was applied for, then turned down, a rejected application.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned down' looks like rejected, but 'down' is NOT UP, and 'turned' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: To apply make-up or a coat of paint is to put it on; a phrasal synonym.

clue.text: Unfed, yell out in way reflecting poverty

indicators.note: out signals the letters are in disarray, thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A hungry, unfed child yells out in a way that shows poverty.
explanation.definitionFit: Being needy is being poor; the adverb describes acting from want or necessity.

clue.text: Old scientist I spotted in sailing ship that's docked

indicators.note: the letter I is seen inside the ship's name
docked means having the tail cut off, so the ship loses its last letter

parts.note: a galleon is a large old sailing ship

explanation.surface: Someone spots an old scientist aboard a sailing ship in port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' suggests a ship in harbour but means cut short: GALLEO, with I inserted.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian astronomer of the early 1600s, a famous scientist of the past.

clue.text: Coverage for scholars from first of government grants

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of government

parts.note: to grant a point is to own or admit it

explanation.surface: Funding for scholars coming chiefly from government grants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grants' looks like money but is the verb: owns, admits.
explanation.definitionFit: Academics wear robes of this kind, so they are what covers scholars.

clue.text: Anger about working with gold as product of mine

indicators.note: about means the word for anger goes round the other pieces

parts.note: ire is anger
on means working, as a machine is on
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A miner angrily working the gold that the mine produces.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock from which a useful metal is extracted is what a mine yields.

clue.text: Installation of minister wrongly nominated without right

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the jumbled letters surround the abbreviation for right
wrongly means the letters of nominated are arranged differently

explanation.surface: A minister was wrongly nominated without having any right to the post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like lacking but means outside: anagram of NOMINATED around R.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister of religion is instituted by being ordained, so the noun is the installing ceremony.

clue.text: Final pieces in the Guardian puzzles you solve come after some time

indicators.note: the final letters of the five words that follow give the answer

explanation.surface: The final parts of the Guardian puzzles you solve fall into place eventually.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to follow on later as a consequence.

clue.text: It conveys how setters continue to show pleasure?

definitions.meaning: a vehicle for carrying goods, a cart

definitions.text: how setters continue to show pleasure
definitions.meaning: setters are dogs, which keep showing pleasure by wagging their tails on and on

explanation.surface: A wry question about how crossword setters keep up their delight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setters' looks like crossword compilers but means the dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A cart for hauling goods conveys them; the second sense is a dog's tail wagging on.

clue.text: In vain, go crazy making name in opera

indicators.note: crazy means the letters of in vain go are mad and jumbled

explanation.surface: Trying in vain to go crazy while making one's name in opera.
explanation.walkthrough: With 19 across this gives Mozart's Don Giovanni.
explanation.definitionFit: Mozart's opera is titled after Don Giovanni, so it is a name in an opera.

clue.text: Sign agreement backing 11 as opposed to 6

indicators.note: backing means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: to nod is to signal yes

explanation.surface: Someone signs an agreement backing one option over another.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 across is PUT ON and 6 down is DOFF: to don clothes is to put them on rather than take them off.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonyms of a sort: to dress in a garment rather than take it off.

clue.text: Having gone off line, what could be deadlier?

indicators.note: what could be signals that deadlier's letters could be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: A train that has left the tracks: what could be more deadly?
explanation.definitionFit: A train that has left its rails has gone off the railway line.

clue.text: Cover body university excepted from constraint

indicators.note: excepted from means taken out of the word for constraint

parts.note: duress is compulsion or constraint

explanation.surface: A university dress code exempting someone from its usual constraints.
explanation.definitionFit: To clothe oneself is to put garments over the body.

clue.text: Power held by male family members, otherwise godfather

indicators.note: held by means the abbreviation for power sits inside the sons

parts.note: sons are male family members
or means otherwise, as in do it or else

explanation.surface: Power held by a mafia family's sons, or else by the godfather himself.
explanation.definitionFit: At a christening a godparent stands as the child's backer, a synonym.

clue.text: Reproduce text about one kiss for romantic hero

indicators.note: about means the word for reproducing text goes round the rest

parts.note: to quote is to repeat someone's words
I is the Roman numeral for one
X stands for a kiss in letters

explanation.surface: Copying out a love letter about a kiss, for a romantic hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Cervantes' Don is an impractical idealist, a romantic hero of chivalry.

clue.text: Put out as check follows piece surrendering centre

indicators.note: follows means the abbreviation for check comes after the piece
surrendering centre means the piece gives up its middle letter

parts.note: the queen is a chess piece
CH is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: A chess move: putting a player in check after giving up a piece in the centre.
explanation.definitionFit: To put out a fire, or a thirst, is to extinguish it.

clue.text: Its rival's sporting gear is a shade lighter

definitions.text: Its rival's sporting gear is a shade lighter

parts.words: Its rival's sporting gear is a shade lighter
parts.note: the varsity rival is Cambridge, whose sporting blue is paler than the dark blue worn by the other university

explanation.surface: A sports team comparing kit colours with its rival's.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Boat Race and other varsity matches, Cambridge wears light blue and the older rival dark blue.
explanation.definitionFit: The English university whose rival Cambridge wears a lighter blue in varsity sport.

clue.text: Turn to play, as I'd a term off

indicators.note: off means the letters are not in their proper order

explanation.surface: A student turns to acting, having a term off.
explanation.definitionFit: To adapt a story for the stage is to turn it into a play.

clue.text: Fortune initially increased tenfold, dear

indicators.note: the first letter, a Roman numeral, is multiplied by ten: 50 becomes 500

parts.note: luck is fortune

explanation.surface: A fortune that increased tenfold at the start, dear.
explanation.walkthrough: L is 50 in Roman numerals; ten times that is 500, D.
explanation.definitionFit: A term of endearment used in northern England, like love or dear.

clue.text: A car carrying head of one state

indicators.note: carrying means the car holds the next letter inside it

parts.note: VW, Volkswagen, is a make of car

indicators.note: head of takes the first letter of one

explanation.surface: A car carrying the head of one state, an official motorcade.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to declare openly.

clue.text: Group of criminals in a car tailed on motorway

indicators.note: on means the car comes after the motorway letter

parts.note: M stands for motorway, as in the M1

indicators.note: tailed means the car loses its last letter

parts.note: a Fiat is a make of car

explanation.surface: Criminals in a car tailed by police on the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailed' looks like followed by police but means its tail removed: FIA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sicilian organised-crime network is the classic criminal gang.

clue.text: Playfully teasing principal (at start of term)

definitions.meaning: mischievous and knowing, sly in a playful way
chief, as a prefix at the start of a term such as archbishop or archenemy

explanation.surface: A head teacher who teases playfully at the start of the school term.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket says the 'principal' sense is used as a prefix at the start of a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: sly and roguish; and chief, as a prefix.

clue.text: Piece of poetry penned by significant other

indicators.note: penned by means held in, enclosed by the following words

explanation.surface: A poem written by one's partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A division of a long poem, such as Dante's Inferno, is called by this term.

clue.text: Odd charmer back without a penny from US

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside: the reversed name goes round the coin
back means the enchantress's name is written in reverse

parts.note: Circe was the enchantress of Greek myth who charmed Odysseus's men
a cent is the American penny

explanation.surface: A strange charmer who has returned from America without a penny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like lacking, but in its old sense means outside, wrapping round the coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: strange, unconventional in behaviour.
